The MK whistleblower

By: Joy Summers | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
We have on-camera interview with self-styled whistleblower Lennox Ntsodo who confesses how he helped to forge signatures to get the MK party on to the ballot paper. But we also test the information he gives us to establish whether he is telling the truth, including testing the evidence he has given us against the names and numbers of 120 people in Steenberg, Cape Town, who were on the list he alleges was submitted to Parliament. This is a development on the story that was broken a fortnight ago when his allegations were first aired.


Summary:
As South Africa approaches an unpredictable and possibly volatile election, explosive allegations expose one of the newest parties on the block. The MK party led by former president Jacob Zuma. This fledgeling party is already mired in controversy not least because its controversial leader Jacob Zuma has threatened to abolish the constitution if he gets elected. Also hanging in the balance is whether or not he can legally lead this party to the polls due to an earlier prison sentence. Now one of his earliest supporters has come forward to reveal how the MK party has allegedly committed electoral fraud by stealing identities in order to meet the requirements to make it onto the ballot.

Further information:
We show how a community leader in Steenberg persuaded people to sign up under false pretences - with the promise of Khoisan funding or a job in Parliament - in order to feed the MK election machinery with signatures needed to get on to the ballot paper. And we confront the MK Party and the IEC about this matter.

Press Release:


Fact or Faction

On the face of it, he’s just a flamboyant character, accustomed to a flashy lifestyle and luxury vehicles. But Lennox Ntsodo, a former high-placed member of uMkhonto weSizwe Political Party, insists he’s a credible whistleblower with shocking allegations about the fledgling movement. As South Africa approaches an unpredictable and possibly volatile election, Carte Blanche examines the evidence for allegations that one of the country’s newest parties committed electoral fraud.

Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Govan Whittles



Script:


MK Whistleblower Script
Producer: Marion Edmunds

(VO1 )OVER THE LAST MONTHS, ONE OF SOUTH AFRICA’s NEWEST POLITICAL PARTIES, THE UMKHONTO WESIZWE PARTY, HAS SURGED IN POPULARITY,
THE MK PARTY HAS COME FROM NOWHERE - TO BEING A SERIOUS CONTENDER FOR POWER.
LED CONTROVERSIALLY BY FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA, IT’S ALSO BEEN DOGGED BY INTRIGUE…

(VO2)
AND A GROUP OF CAPETONIANS DISCOVERED THIS WEEK THAT THEY’VE BEEN DUPED INTO ENDORSING MK - A PARTY THEY DO NOT SUPPORT.

ASTRID ISAACS
Steenberg resident
That’s my signature, that’s my handwriting…. But what is happening there on top?
Govan: That’s the party name, that’s the party name
Astrid: I see yes that but this top looks very sketchy now.

(VO3) NEW POLITICAL PARTIES ARE REQUIRED TO PROVE THEIR SUPPORT TO GET ON TO THE BALLOT.
TO DO THAT THEY NEED THE NAMES, ID NUMBERS AND SIGNATURES OF THOUSANDS OF SUPPORTERS.
AND MK STANDS ACCUSED OF FORGING AT LEAST SOME OF THESE LISTS.

GW: That’s your ID number?
CA: Yes and my telephone number.
GW: Is that your signature there?
CA: Yes.
GW: It is?
CA:It is!

(VO4) 
AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION AROUND HIS IDENTITY - A FORMER MK PARTY OFFICIAL TURNED WHISTLEBLOWER AGREED TO TALK TO US .
(VO4) OUR SOURCE WAS EVEN PREPARED TO DO AN ON-CAMERA INTERVIEW TO EXPLAIN HOW HE HAD FACILITATED IDENTITY THEFT TO GET THE MK PARTY ON TO THE BALLOT PAPER.

(VO5) BY THEN, HE’D ALREADY REPORTED HIMSELF TO THE POLICE, CLAIMING THIS WRONGDOING WAS, ALLEGEDLY INSTIGATED BY MK LEADERS. HIS NAME IS LENNOX NTSODO.

LENNOX NTSODO
Former MK Party Western Cape Organiser
I'm talking about them asking us to go to the database of the City of Cape Town, to download job seekers forms, and also rewrite the names and forge signatures of those people in the IEC forms.

GW: Why?

LN: Because they couldl not reach the target of - they said we must have around 7500 signatures to be on the ballot paper for province and national. So we have to forge the signature on that form to submit to the IEC.

(VO6) LENNOX SAID HE HAD PERSUADED GROUPS OF ABOUT TWENTY VOLUNTEERS FROM HIS NEIGHBOURHOOD TO COPY LISTS OF NAMES, AND FORGE SIGNATURES ALLEGEDLY FROM A CONFIDENTIAL DATABASE, OVER A TWO WEEK PERIOD. HE SAYS THOSE WERE SENT ON TO MK HEAD OFFICE TO BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEC.

SY MAMABOLA SOUND UP: The MK signature issue is still under police investigation….

(VO7) FROM THE GET GO, THE SIGNATURE REQUIREMENT WAS FLAGGED AS PROBLEMATIC BY THE INDEPENDENT ELECTORAL COMMISSION, SAYS CHIEF ELECTORAL OFFICER SY MAMABOLO

SY MAMABOLO
CHIEF ELECTORAL OFFICER, IEC
The IEC questioned Parliament to say there is no earthly way in which you can verify whether the signature is the is of the person that is purported to have to have made it. So in that context, the IEC can only look at whether the person is alive, is a South African citizen and whether it's a registered voter, those are the the checks that the IEC is capable of making.

GW: So you suspected you might end up in this very position.
SM: We did question Parliament about it in the portfolio committee already.

(VO10) AND IN THIS CONFLICTED SPACE, FLAMBOYANT POLITICAL OPERATOR, LENNOX NTSODO, HAS SET OFF A POLITICAL LANDMINE

GW:07:53 See, you've you've got a whistleblower here alleging forging of signatures for one party in the Western Cape. And the obvious question is, well, could this have been the case for other parties?

SY MAMABOLO 8:47 Suspicions, innuendo, this and that is not going to help the process. What will help the process is to have an independent investigation of the allegations

(VO11 ) WE SET OUT TO VERIFY THE INFORMATION LENNOX - OR LENNY AS HE’S KNOWN - LEAKED TO US ON THIS LIST.

GOVAN WHITTLES: It’s in this Cape Town Suburb, Steenberg, that most of the people on Lenny’s list appear to live. Yet we have been told that the MK Party has very little presence here.

(VO12) WE SHOWED THE LIST TO CHANTEL ADAMS.
WHILE RECOGNISING HER DETAILS AND SIGNATURE, SHE INITIALLY HAD NO RECOLLECTION OF ENDORSING MK.
AND THEN - IT ALL CAME BACK TO HER.

CHANTEL ADAMS
Steenberg Resident
This guy told us the Khoisan has got money, and we are entitled to that money. That is what he told us.
GW: For the Khoisan?
CA: …we are supposed to give, I don’t know how much for a Khoisan ID, we are going to get a new ID and everything.

(VO13) IN OTHER WORDS SHE HAD BEEN TRICKED INTO SIGNING UNDER FALSE PRETENCES.

(VO14)SO WE PUT THE ALLEGATIONS OF FRAUD TO MK’S SPOKESPERSON, NHLAMULO NDHLELA, AND SHOWED HIM THE LIST WE WERE WORKING FROM.

11:39 GOVAN WHITTLES: I'd like you to have a look at this for me, please. …. these are the ones that Lennox Ntsodo -
NN: we're told that they are fraudulent and as I say until the investigation is done, we will know if they are MK forms are not.
GW: But those are legitimate MK forms?
NN: From the looks of it. Yes.

NHLAMULO NDHLELA
Spokesperson, UMKHONTO WESIZWE Party (MKP)
We are the victim here. The person that ought to be disqualified.,and this is what we need to investigate - is this saboteur.

GW: But Lennox is not contesting the election, MK party is.

NN: No, but - But that's exactly the point.

GW: But he was not doing it for the MK party?

NN:He was doing it for his own agenda. That's why all of a sudden now he wants to come out in public and say that, you know, MK party forged signatures when he's the one who forged the signatures.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Lennox Ntsodo is a complex character. He is currently out on bail after being charged with fraud in a case running here at the Blue Downs Magistrate’s Court. He’s accused of illegally selling plots of land in Mfuleni for a hundred thousand rand each.

(VO15) AND LENNOX ALSO HAS POLITICAL ASPIRATIONS.
HE IS CURRENTLY HIGH UP ON MK’s WESTERN CAPE PROVINCIAL PARLIAMENTARY LIST. ACCORDING TO MK, THIS IS WHAT IT’s ALL ABOUT.

NHLAMULO NDHLELA
Spokesperson, UMKHONTO WESIZWE Party (MKP)
I've even got confirmation of recordings and calls that he has made, he wanted to be number one, on the candidate under parliamentary list for a provincial level, if not, then you must at least be at national, of which we then upon reviewing exactly who this person is, then realised that we cannot afford to do so.

(VO16) WE ASKED STEENBERG RESIDENTS ASTRID ISAACS AND HER FRIEND TASNEEMAH PAULSE WHY THEIR NAMES APPEARED ON THE MK LIST DESPITE NOT BEING ZUMA SUPPORTERS.

ASTRID ISAACS
Steenberg Resident
But what was that, they were going to get a job in Parliament. Every one of them needed 25 signatures. They're gonna get jobs in Parliament. Can you recall that! You are going to get jobs in Parliament yeah!

(VO15)ASTRID KNEW MANY OF THE NAMES HERE - NEIGHBOURS WHO THOUGHT THEY WERE SIGNING UP FOR JOBS BUT ENDED UP ON AN MK LIST.

GOVAN WHITTLES IN CAR: So we have been directed to a church near by because the pastor there is apparently the person who got everyone to sign up.

GW: Can we come inside?

(VO17) PASTOR SAMUEL PETERSEN WAS BUSY RENOVATING HIS CHURCH

GW: You, told Chantal Adams to sign this form, isn't that right?
Sam Petersen: Yeah. I remember this form now. Yeah. Secretary General, IEC.
GW: This is an endorsement form, for the MK party: Isn't that right?
Sam Petersen: I don't know. I don't know. I was just given this form. And say, and I was told to ask people to sign.

(VO18) PASTOR SAM CONTACTED THE ATTORNEY WHO HAD GIVEN HIM THE LISTS. THE ATTORNEY CONFIRMED HE WAS ASKED TO GET SIGNATURES FOR MK, BUT REFUSED TO SAY BY WHOM.

Sam Petersen: I knew that the form said MK, but I was told that the MK works with the Khoisans.

GW: What?

SP: Ja

(VO19) AS THE ELECTIONS APPROACH, FORMER PRESIDENT JACOB ZUMA HAS BEEN CAMPAIGNING AROUND THE COUNTRY FOR HIS PARTY.

GW: The President did travel to the Western Cape. When he went there, what was his his campaign or his programme like?

NN: So President went to firstly meet up with the Khoisan leadership, …. he had a number of meetings regarding the Western Cape for strategic purposes.

LENNOX NTSODO
Former WC UMKHONTO WESIZWE PARTY ORGANISER
I was the one who was running around organising for funds for him. … you must host the President,

GW: What kind of hosting are we talking about there?

LN: Accommodation, you must host him with food and also when he goes home, you must have a parcel that you must hand over him because we as the Western Cape we've organised 50k for him to go with home because they said the President don't have money. So, yes.

(VO20) AGAIN, MK DENIES THIS IS TRUE.

17:30 NN: what he says we ought to be taking with a pinch of salt.

(VO21) LATE THIS WEEK, WE WERE STILL WAITING FOR EVIDENCE TO BACK UP LENNY’s ORIGINAL ALLEGATIONS THAT HE WAS INVOLVED IN STEALING IDENTITIES FROM THE CITY’s JOBSEEKERS DATABASE. AFTER LYING LOW FOR A FEW DAYS, HE ANSWERED HIS PHONE.

GOVAN WHITTLES ON THE PHONE: So Lenny, the MK party says that you plan to do this all along. It was your intention to submit forged signatures and you didn't work with anyone in the leadership, you did it by yourself and you actually just fooled them, that they weren't working with you at all?

LENNOX NTSODO VOICE ON PHONE: I will show you a video where they were recorded, and were sitting, forging signatures.

GOVAN WHITTLES: With whom, with the MK Party?

LENNOX NTSODO VOICE ON PHONE: With the MK Party - all of them.

(VO22) LENNY SENT US VIDEOS AND PHOTOS - WHILE PLACING HIM AT THE CENTRE OF THE MK CAMPAIGN, THEY DON’T, ON THEIR OWN, PROVE THE ALLEGATIONS. HE SAYS HE’S HANDED THIS INFORMATION TO THE POLICE AND THE IEC.

GOVAN WHITTLES: Never before in South Africa has a president returned to Parliament as an MP for another party. And if he succeeds, Jacob Zuma’s return may be more controversial than his exit.

(VO23) THIS WEEKEND THE MK PARTY CAME OUT WITH A SHOW OF STRENGTH IN SOWETO - A MESSAGE THAT ON ELECTION DAY, IT WILL BE A FORCE TO BE RECKONED WITH. YET, WITH THESE ALLEGATIONS IN THE OPEN AS WELL AS MULTIPLE LEGAL CONTROVERSIES, TWO WEEKS IS A LONG TIME IN POLITICS.




PROMO 1

LENNOX NTSODO VOICE ON PHONE: I will show you a video where they were recorded, and were sitting, forging signatures.
GOVAN WHITTLES: With whom, with the MK Party?
(VO1) A FLAMBOYANT WHISTLEBLOWER DROPS A BOMBSHELL
ALLEGING ELECTORAL FRAUD

metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have on-camera interview with self-styled whistleblower Lennox Ntsodo who confesses how he helped to forge signatures to get the MK party on to the ballot paper. But we also test the information he gives us to establish whether he is telling the truth, including testing the evidence he has given us against the names and numbers of 120 people in Steenberg, Cape Town, who were on the list he alleges was submitted to Parliament. This is a development on the story that was broken a fortnight ago when his allegations were first aired.
metadata.Summary: As South Africa approaches an unpredictable and possibly volatile election, explosive allegations expose one of the newest parties on the block. The MK party led by former president Jacob Zuma. This fledgeling party is already mired in controversy not least because its controversial leader Jacob Zuma has threatened to abolish the constitution if he gets elected. Also hanging in the balance is whether or not he can legally lead this party to the polls due to an earlier prison sentence. Now one of his earliest supporters has come forward to reveal how the MK party has allegedly committed electoral fraud by stealing identities in order to meet the requirements to make it onto the ballot.
metadata.Further information: We show how a community leader in Steenberg persuaded people to sign up under false pretences - with the promise of Khoisan funding or a job in Parliament - in order to feed the MK election machinery with signatures needed to get on to the ballot paper. And we confront the MK Party and the IEC about this matter.
